fullPassage: What do you think good design is? Some might assert good design makes products easy to use, while others might say good design is stylish or innovative. There are even some who believe that good design should be as environmentally friendly as possible. All of these are important elements of design. However, there is a new idea called “universal design.” This idea suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty looks and functions. Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people and includes features that make it possible for them to access and use products without any barriers. Now let’s take a look at how universal design is tackling the problem of limited access and reshaping the design of products and services. Universal design suggests that design be as flexible as possible so that it can accommodate diverse needs and a wide range of individual preferences. This could involve providing a variety of options for customization or adding adjustable features to a product. Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk pictured below. Do you notice how they differ from the more common types of scissors, mice, and desks? They are all designed for left-handed people. Without them, about 10% of the world’s population, who are left-handed, would find these simple products difficult to use. The height-adjustable desk is also a good example of a universal design that accommodates a wide range of individual preferences and abilities. If the desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it to the heights they want. If desired, the user can work while standing. A wheelchair user is also able to use the desk at a comfortable height. Universal design also ensures that an environment or product is accessible to everyone. Anyone should be able to use a design regardless of who they are and what they’re capable of, and no one should be excluded. Curb cuts are a good example. Without curb cuts, people in wheelchairs would have a hard time navigating the city. Curb cuts eliminate barriers not only for wheelchair users but also for people moving heavy loads or riding bikes. Like curb cuts, automatic doors in public buildings also allow all people to enter without any major problems. Another characteristic of universal design is requiring low physical effort. Universal design seeks to create products that can be used efficiently and comfortably without causing unnecessary fatigue. Undoubtedly, many people have had trouble trying to open a lid of a jar that was stuck. Opening a lid can be a great challenge to people with a weak grip, the elderly, or people with hand or finger impairments. Fortunately, various clever opening devices have been designed. A lever-type door handle, which requires no firm grip or twisting, is also an example that reflects this characteristic of universal design. A door with a lever-type door handle can be opened using an elbow or a closed hand, which benefits people carrying baskets as well as those with limited strength in their hands. Universal design is not limited to the design of physical products or facilities. Universal design pushes for designs in which critical information is conveyed well, regardless of the surrounding environment or the user’s sensory abilities. Information should be conveyed not just through written language but also through universal symbols and audio cues. For instance, when it comes to foreign travelers, finding a restroom is much easier when they can simply look for the universally recognized restroom symbol rather than trying to interpret the local language. For those with visual or audio impairments, bus and subway arrival times are not only presented on electronic boards but also called out through voice announcements. In elevators, braille, which indicates the floor number, allows individuals with visual impairments to select their desired floor. Additionally, audio announcements confirm the selected floor and tell passengers when the elevator has reached their desired floor. As such, providing information in these diverse forms ensures that everyone can access and understand important information, regardless of language barriers, sensory impairments, etc. Universal design is beneficial to everyone. With universal design, no one needs to put up with unnecessary discomfort. The supporters of universal design suggest that it should be part of every design. Take a look around you. Is there anything that needs improvement so that it can be accessible to more people? If so, why not create a design and bring joy to more people?

버스와 지하철의 도착 시간은 음성으로는 전혀 안내되지 않는다.

questions.passage: What do you think good design is?  Some might assert good design makes products easy to use, while others might say good design is stylish or innovative.  There are even some who believe that good design should be as environmentally friendly as possible.  All of these are important elements of design.  However, there is a new idea called “universal design. ” This idea suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty looks and functions.  Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people and includes features that make it possible for them to access and use products without any barriers.  Now let’s take a look at how universal design is tackling the problem of limited access and reshaping the design of products and services.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 글 전체를 아우르는 중심 소재.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 왼손잡이 제품은 하나의 예시일 뿐 인구 비율·시장 규모가 주제가 아님

❌ ② 자동문·커브컷의 예산 문제는 본문에 없는 내용

❌ ③ 전통 대 현대 디자인의 우열은 글의 초점이 아님

✅ ④ 유니버설 디자인이 유연성·접근성·낮은 신체적 노력·정보 전달을 통해 다양한 사람이 장벽 없이 쓰게 한다는 것이 글 전체의 주제 ← 정답
det.tip: 유연성·접근성·낮은 노력·정보 전달 네 특징을 관통하는 것이 유니버설 디자인입니다.

ch: 왼손잡이 인구 비율과 그에 따른 제품 시장 규모의 변화
공공장소에 자동문과 커브컷을 설치하는 데 드는 예산 문제
전통적인 디자인이 현대 디자인보다 우수하다고 평가되는 이유

questions.passage: What do you think good design is?  Some might assert good design makes products easy to use, while others might say good design is stylish or innovative.  There are even some who believe that good design should be as environmentally friendly as possible.  All of these are important elements of design.  However, there is a new idea called “universal design. ” This idea suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty looks and functions.  Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people and includes features that make it possible for them to access and use products without any barriers.  Now let’s take a look at how universal design is tackling the problem of limited access and reshaping the design of products and services.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ③ Design for All: Removing Barriers for Everyone(모두를 위한 디자인: 모두의 장벽 없애기)
det.analysis:
글은 유니버설 디자인이 다양한 사람의 요구를 반영해 누구도 배제되지 않게 장벽을 없앤다는 내용이에요.

❌ ① Left-Handed Tools: A Niche Market's Rise(왼손잡이 도구: 틈새시장의 부상): 왼손잡이 제품은 예시일 뿐, 시장 이야기가 아니에요.

❌ ② Why Pretty Looks Matter Most in Design(왜 디자인에서 예쁜 외양이 가장 중요한가): 본문은 오히려 겉모습을 '넘어서야' 한다고 해요.

✅ ③ Design for All: Removing Barriers for Everyone(모두를 위한 디자인: 모두의 장벽 없애기): 다양한 사용자가 장벽 없이 접근·사용하게 한다는 글 전체를 압축한 제목이에요 ← 정답

❌ ④ The History of Automatic Doors in Cities(도시 자동문의 역사): 자동문은 하나의 예시일 뿐 역사 이야기가 아니에요.
det.tip: 핵심 메시지 = 모두를 위해 장벽을 없애는 디자인(Design for All)

ch: Left-Handed Tools: A Niche Market's Rise

questions.passage: However, there is a new idea called “universal design. ” This idea suggests that design should <u>go beyond mere pretty looks and functions</u>.  Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people and includes features that make it possible for them to access and use products without any barriers.  Now let’s take a look at how universal design is tackling the problem of limited access and reshaping the design of products and services.  Universal design suggests that design be as flexible as possible so that it can accommodate diverse needs and a wide range of individual preferences.  This could involve providing a variety of options for customization or adding adjustable features to a product.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 go beyond mere pretty looks and functions가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② 디자인은 겉모습과 기능을 넘어 더 넓은 사용성과 포용까지 담아야 한다는 것
det.analysis:
밑줄 문장: 'This idea suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty looks and functions.'(이 생각은 디자인이 그저 예쁜 겉모습과 기능을 '넘어서야' 한다고 제안한다). 'go beyond ~'는 '~ 그 이상으로 나아가다'라는 뜻으로, 겉모습·기능에 머물지 말고 더 나아가라는 의미예요.

❌ ① '충분하다'는 것은 '넘어서라(go beyond)'는 뜻과 정반대예요.

✅ ② 겉모습과 기능을 넘어 다양한 사람이 쓸 수 있는 사용성·포용까지 담아야 한다는 뜻이에요. 바로 뒤에 '다양한 요구를 고려한다'는 설명이 이어져요. ←정답

❌ ③ 기능이 중요하지 않다는 말은 본문에 없어요.

❌ ④ 예술성을 편의보다 우선하라는 내용은 없어요.
det.tip: go beyond ~ = ~을 넘어서다 → 겉모습·기능 그 이상(포용·사용성)까지

ch: 디자인은 예쁜 겉모습과 기능만 갖추면 그것으로 충분하다는 것
디자인은 겉모습과 기능을 넘어 더 넓은 사용성과 포용까지 담아야 한다는 것
디자인에서 기능은 중요하지 않고 오직 외양만 중요하다는 것
디자인은 사용자의 편의보다 예술적 아름다움을 우선해야 한다는 것

questions.passage: This could involve providing a variety of options for customization or adding adjustable features to a product.  Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk pictured below.  Do you notice how <u>they</u> differ from the more common types of scissors, mice, and desks?  They are all designed for left-handed people.  Without them, about 10% of the world’s population, who are left-handed, would find these simple products difficult to use.  The height-adjustable desk is also a good example of a universal design that accommodates a wide range of individual preferences and abilities.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 they가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① 아래 그림에 나온 가위, 컴퓨터 마우스, 책상
det.analysis:
밑줄 문장: 'Do you notice how ___ differ from the more common types of scissors, mice, and desks?'(___이 더 흔한 종류의 가위, 마우스, 책상과 어떻게 다른지 알겠는가?). 바로 앞 문장 'Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk pictured below.'에서 소개한 '아래 그림 속 가위·마우스·책상'을 they가 받아요.

✅ ① 아래 그림에 나온 가위, 컴퓨터 마우스, 책상: 앞 문장에서 언급한 바로 그 세 제품이에요 ←정답

❌ ② '흔한 종류'는 they가 그것과 '다르다'고 비교되는 대상이라 they 자체가 아니에요.

❌ ③ 전 세계 인구의 10%는 뒤 문장에 나오는 다른 대상이에요.

❌ ④ 책상 한 가지가 아니라 세 제품 모두를 가리켜요.
det.tip: 앞 문장의 the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk를 they가 받습니다.

ch: 아래 그림에 나온 가위, 컴퓨터 마우스, 책상
높이 조절이 되는 책상 한 가지

questions.passage: Another characteristic of universal design is requiring __________.  Universal design seeks to create products that can be used efficiently and comfortably without causing unnecessary fatigue.  Undoubtedly, many people have had trouble trying to open a lid of a jar that was stuck.  Opening a lid can be a great challenge to people with a weak grip, the elderly, or people with hand or finger impairments.  Fortunately, various clever opening devices have been designed.  A lever-type door handle, which requires no firm grip or twisting, is also an example that reflects this characteristic of universal design.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 빈칸에 low physical effort(낮은 신체적 노력)가 적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① a large storage space(넓은 수납 공간): 뒤이어 나오는 '효율적·편안하게, 불필요한 피로 없이'와 무관

❌ ② constant human help(끊임없는 사람의 도움): 오히려 도움 없이도 쓸 수 있게 한다는 흐름과 반대

❌ ③ high financial cost(높은 금전적 비용): 비용이 아니라 '신체적 노력'에 관한 문단

✅ ④ low physical effort(낮은 신체적 노력): 바로 뒤 문장에서 '효율적이고 편안하게, 불필요한 피로 없이' 쓰인다고 했으므로, 이 특징은 '낮은 신체적 노력'이에요 ← 정답
det.tip: used efficiently and comfortably without causing unnecessary fatigue → low physical effort(낮은 신체적 노력)

questions.passage: This could involve providing a variety of options for customization or adding adjustable features to a product.  Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk pictured below.  Do you notice how they differ from the more common types of scissors, mice, and desks?  __________.  Without them, about 10% of the world’s population, who are left-handed, would find these simple products difficult to use.  The height-adjustable desk is also a good example of a universal design that accommodates a wide range of individual preferences and abilities.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"그것들은 모두 왼손잡이를 위해 설계되었다." (7단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) all, are, designed, for, left-handed, people, they 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 7단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: They are all designed for left-handed people
det.analysis:
'그것들은 ~ 설계되었다'는 '~되다'라는 수동의 뜻이라 수동태(be + 과거분사)로 써요.

주어는 They(그것들은)이고, 동사는 'are + designed'(설계되었다)예요. '모두'를 뜻하는 all은 be동사 뒤에 넣어요: They + are + all + designed.

'왼손잡이를 위해'는 for left-handed people로 써요: for + left-handed + people.

순서대로 이으면 They / are / all / designed / for / left-handed / people.
det.tip: 수동태 are designed(설계되었다) + all은 be동사 뒤에: are all designed

questions.wa: They are all designed for left-handed people
accept: They are all designed for left-handed people

questions.passage: Universal design suggests that design be as flexible as possible so that it can accommodate diverse needs and a wide range of individual preferences.  This could involve providing a variety of options for customization or adding adjustable features to a product.  Take a look at the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk ①<u>picturing</u> below.  Do you notice how they differ from the more common types of scissors, mice, and desks?  They are all designed for left-handed people.  Without them, about 10% of the world’s population, who are left-handed, would find these simple products difficult to use.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀렸다. 어법에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오. (한 단어, 영어로)

det.korean: picturing → pictured: 'the desk (which is) pictured below'로 명사를 뒤에서 꾸미는 과거분사이므로 pictured
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 부분은 'the scissors, the computer mouse, and the desk ①<u>picturing</u> below'예요. '아래에 그려진(사진으로 실린) 가위, 마우스, 책상'이라는 뜻이에요.

여기서 책상은 스스로 '그리는' 것이 아니라 그림·사진으로 '그려진(실린)' 대상이에요. 그래서 명사를 뒤에서 꾸미는 과거분사 pictured(그려진)로 써야 해요. 'the desk (which is) pictured below(아래에 실린 책상)'로 이해하면 돼요.

picturing(현재분사)은 능동이라 뜻이 어긋나 틀려요. 정답은 pictured예요.
det.tip: 명사 뒤에서 '~된'은 과거분사: the desk pictured below(아래에 실린 책상)

questions.passage: They are all designed for left-handed people.  Without them, about 10% of the world’s population, who are left-handed, would find these simple products difficult to use.  __________ that accommodates a wide range of individual preferences and abilities.  If the desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it to the heights they want.  If desired, the user can work while standing.  A wheelchair user is also able to use the desk at a comfortable height.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"높이 조절 책상 또한 유니버설 디자인의 좋은 예이다." (12단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) a, a, also, design, desk, example, good, height-adjustable, is, of, the, universal 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 12단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: The height-adjustable desk is also a good example of a universal design
det.analysis:
'A는 또한 B의 좋은 예이다'는 'A is also a good example of B' 구조로 써요.

먼저 주어는 '높이 조절 책상'이에요. 관사 The를 붙여 The height-adjustable desk로 써요: The + height-adjustable + desk.

동사와 '또한'은 is also로 이어요: is + also.

'좋은 예'는 a good example, '~의'는 of로 연결해요: a + good + example + of.

'유니버설 디자인'은 a universal design으로 마무리해요: a + universal + design.

순서대로 이으면 The / height-adjustable / desk / is / also / a / good / example / of / a / universal / design.
det.tip: A is also a good example of B(A 또한 B의 좋은 예이다) 구조

questions.wa: The height-adjustable desk is also a good example of a universal design
accept: The height-adjustable desk is also a good example of a universal design

questions.passage: The height-adjustable desk is also a good example of a universal design that accommodates a wide range of individual preferences and abilities.  If the desk is too high or too low, the users can adjust it to the heights they want.  If desired, the user can work while standing.  __________.  Universal design also ensures that an environment or product is accessible to everyone.  Anyone should be able to use a design regardless of who they are and what they’re capable of, and no one should be excluded.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
"휠체어 사용자도 편안한 높이에서 그 책상을 사용할 수 있다."

[ a / a / able / also / at / comfortable / desk / height / is / the / to / use / user / wheelchair ] (14단어) (영어로)

det.korean: A wheelchair user is also able to use the desk at a comfortable height
det.analysis:
먼저 주어는 '휠체어 사용자'예요: A + wheelchair + user.

'~도 …할 수 있다'는 'be also able to + 동사원형'으로 써요: is + also + able + to + use.

무엇을 쓰는가 하면 목적어 '그 책상'이에요: the + desk.

'편안한 높이에서'는 전치사구로 문장 뒤에 놓아요: at + a + comfortable + height.

순서대로 이으면 A / wheelchair / user / is / also / able / to / use / the / desk / at / a / comfortable / height.
det.tip: be able to(~할 수 있다) + at a comfortable height(편안한 높이에서)

questions.wa: A wheelchair user is also able to use the desk at a comfortable height
accept: A wheelchair user is also able to use the desk at a comfortable height

questions.passage: However, there is a new idea called “universal design. ” This idea suggests that design should go beyond mere pretty looks and functions.  __________ and includes features that make it possible for them to access and use products without any barriers.  Now let’s take a look at how universal design is tackling the problem of limited access and reshaping the design of products and services.  Universal design suggests that design be as flexible as possible so that it can accommodate diverse needs and a wide range of individual preferences.  This could involve providing a variety of options for customization or adding adjustable features to a product.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"유니버설 디자인은 서로 다른 사람들의 다양한 요구를 고려한다." (11단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) account, design, different, diverse, into, needs, of, people, takes, the, universal 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 11단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people
det.analysis:
'~을 고려하다'는 'take into account ~'라는 굳어진 표현이에요. 주어가 단수(Universal design)라 takes로 써요: Universal + design + takes + into + account.

무엇을 고려하는가 하면 '서로 다른 사람들의 다양한 요구'예요. '다양한 요구'는 the diverse needs, '서로 다른 사람들의'는 of different people로 이어요: the + diverse + needs + of + different + people.

순서대로 이으면 Universal / design / takes / into / account / the / diverse / needs / of / different / people.
det.tip: take into account(~을 고려하다) + the diverse needs of different people(서로 다른 사람들의 다양한 요구)

questions.wa: Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people
accept: Universal design takes into account the diverse needs of different people
